Q: Adaptive Icon not working A:

1st time I tried, it worked but I got an ugly icon, obviously based on mine

Later when I tried to tidy it up, I now just get the default Icon (looks like it's failing)

Tired various things, inc "clean project" , no joy

There is a Google HOWTO:

From: https://developer.android.com/codelabs/basic-android-kotlin-compose-training-change-app-icon#4

So downloaded the "solution" to the exercise, (https://github.com/google-developer-training/basic-android-kotlin-compose-training-affirmations/archive/refs/heads/main.zip ) note this contains:

Looking in


...app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:

        android:icon="@mipmap/ic_launcher"

However, there is NO ...res/mipmap directory

However in the directory res/drawable:

...
  -rw-rw-r--  1 android android  1350 Jan 10  2025 ic_launcher_background.xml
  -rw-rw-r--  1 android android  2968 Jan 10  2025 ic_launcher_foreground.xml

If I take these two files and copy them into MY app in res/drawable

Then it "works" ...** sort of** , the new "blue flower" icon appears on my device but there is an error in AndroidStudio:

string too large to encode using UTF-8 written instead as 'STRING_TOO_LARGE'. Ask Gemini

So while the HOWTO makes it clear the files should go in res/mipmap:

  1. The example app puts them in res/drawable (and it works)
  2. The "Image Asset" tool in Android studio saves the generated file in res/drawable (it offers no choice of location)

I also tried the "trick" @Mikel used , I added a TextView of it .... but this simply cause the app to fail to launch, even in debug mode ...@Mikel** is there some "magic way" you accessed that error message **java.lang.IllegalArgumentException:

So, in summary, the docs are wrong . It appears if there are any "errors" in your res/drawable/ic_launcher* files you get the default icon. However the "Image Asset" is quite happy with it and it displays just fine. It would be useful if this tool checked the file it generates id "good".

Q: /usr/bin/arm-none-eabi-ld: error: crt0.o: conflicting use of R9 A:

I was able to resolve my issue by systematically removing source files and command line parameters until I isolated this issue. Since I didn't find any other mentions of this problem, I created this question & answer.

The following setup reproduces the issue:

// Example.c

int main(int argc, char **argv, char **envp)
{
    return 0;
}

# crt0.S

.syntax unified
.cpu cortex-m0plus
.thumb

.extern _main

.global _start
.thumb_func
_start:
    bl _start

# problem.sh

clang \
    --target=arm-none-eabi \
    -mcpu=cortex-m0plus \
    -nostdlib \
    -fropi \
    -frwpi \
    /home/me/dev/pico-os/Userland/Example.c \
    /home/me/dev/pico-os/Userland/LibC/sys/crt0.S \
    -c

clang \
    --target=arm-none-eabi \
    -mcpu=cortex-m0plus \
    -nostdlib \
    -fropi \
    -frwpi \
    ./Example.o \
    ./crt0.o \
    -o Example.elf

$ ./problem.sh 
/usr/bin/arm-none-eabi-ld: error: ./crt0.o: conflicting use of R9
/usr/bin/arm-none-eabi-ld: failed to merge target specific data of file ./crt0.o
/usr/bin/arm-none-eabi-ld: warning: ./crt0.o: missing .note.GNU-stack section implies executable stack
/usr/bin/arm-none-eabi-ld: NOTE: This behaviour is deprecated and will be removed in a future version of the linker
clang: error: linker command failed with exit code 1 (use -v to see invocation)

The problem can be diagnosed by inspecting the object files with readelf:

$ arm-none-eabi-readelf --arch-specific ./Example.o 
Attribute Section: aeabi
File Attributes
  Tag_conformance: "2.09"
  Tag_CPU_name: "cortex-m0plus"
  Tag_CPU_arch: v6S-M
  Tag_CPU_arch_profile: Microcontroller
  Tag_ARM_ISA_use: No
  Tag_THUMB_ISA_use: Thumb-1
  Tag_ABI_PCS_R9_use: SB
  Tag_ABI_PCS_RW_data: SB-relative
  Tag_ABI_PCS_RO_data: PC-relative
  Tag_ABI_PCS_GOT_use: direct
  Tag_ABI_PCS_wchar_t: 4
  Tag_ABI_FP_denormal: Needed
  Tag_ABI_FP_exceptions: Unused
  Tag_ABI_FP_number_model: IEEE 754
  Tag_ABI_align_needed: 8-byte
  Tag_ABI_align_preserved: 8-byte, except leaf SP
  Tag_ABI_enum_size: int
  Tag_ABI_optimization_goals: Aggressive Debug
  Tag_CPU_unaligned_access: None
  Tag_ABI_FP_16bit_format: IEEE 754
~/dev/pico-os/Build (me)
$ arm-none-eabi-readelf --arch-specific ./crt0.o 
Attribute Section: aeabi
File Attributes
  Tag_CPU_name: "cortex-m0plus"
  Tag_CPU_arch: v6S-M
  Tag_CPU_arch_profile: Microcontroller
  Tag_ARM_ISA_use: No
  Tag_THUMB_ISA_use: Thumb-1
  Tag_CPU_unaligned_access: None

The -fropi and -frwpi options cause the Tag_ABI_PCS_R9_use, Tag_ABI_PCS_RW_data and Tag_ABI_PCS_RO_data attributes to be emitted by the C compiler.

However, this doesn't seem to happen for the assembly file. The linker then complains that the object files are incompatible since the assembly object file has the default Tag_ABI_PCS_R9_use = 0 set, which is incompatible (source).

The solution is to add these attributes manually in the assembly file as well:

.eabi_attribute Tag_ABI_PCS_R9_use, 1
.eabi_attribute Tag_ABI_PCS_RW_data, 2
.eabi_attribute Tag_ABI_PCS_RO_data, 1

An alternative would be to not use -fropi and -frwpi, however, this was not an option for me.
